description: Business invariants and the tests that check each against an independent oracle (SQL written in the test from the documented definition, or numbers worked out by hand). 'kind' says what the evidence is: numerical (a result value compared with an oracle), behavioural (an outcome such as a refusal or isolation, no value), or plan-only. tests/unit/test_invariant_coverage.py fails if a referenced test does not exist. docs/COVERAGE_BY_INVARIANT.md is generated from this file by scripts/coverage_report.py.

invariants.statement: Paid volume is distributor data for company brands only; free drug and market data never enter it
Equivalents are packs times the product's conversion factor, per strength
Revenue is the sum of the per-transaction WAC amount, not volume times a price

A ratio's numerator and denominator cover one population: brand share in its own market (inferred from our products when none is named), segment share within the same markets, PAP within the same products, 340B within the same population with the 340B condition lifted
A ratio over several groups is recomputed from summed components, never averaged; a zero or missing denominator is undefined, never 0 or an error
A count of facilities on record is not time-bounded and counts facilities only; a count of facilities with sales is time-bounded and strictly smaller
Accounts roll up to the top organization with a standalone fallback; grouping is by id, so equal names stay apart
Territories plus the unmapped remainder partition the total; 340B include equals exclude plus only
A threshold's operator decides whether the account exactly at the bound is in; the two sides partition every account
Named windows follow the documented offsets (R6M prior is not six months); series are dense on the reporting calendar at month, quarter and week grain
A period a source did not cover is unknown, never zero; a covered period with no rows is zero
A rolling average averages a full window, reaching before the requested window, and is blank rather than shorter where history runs out
Each period against the one before it: prior from the period before the window, none for the first period of the data, no percentage from a zero or negative prior, per group
Growth is relative change between two windows; share change is in percentage points
A follow-up on 'those accounts' applies the whole cohort, not the displayed page
Row scope and pricing follow the user's CURRENT role, territory and pricing flag, in every shape, with nonempty scopes
Scope binds by territory and region name, so a geography reusing a name is refused at load
A question is answered from one published generation; a refresh between planning and execution is refused, never mixed
invariants.gap: No test compares an answer's VALUES before and after a republication with an oracle on each generation; isolation is proved, value correctness across a republish is inferred from the per-generation oracles

invariants.statement: Every received record reconciles to accepted, quarantined, ignored replay or rejected; corrections apply once, tombstones hold out of order, totals move by exactly the applied changes

not_numerical.planning_explain: tests/integration/test_compatibility_matrix.py: 672 metric x grain x filter x comparison combinations are refused by name or compile, validate and are planned by PostgreSQL (EXPLAIN). No value is checked.
not_numerical.offline_evaluation: evals/*.yaml with the deterministic offline planner: compilation, authorization, execution and rendering of plans the offline planner produces. Not natural-language accuracy.
not_numerical.live_adapter: tests/unit/test_live_adapter_contract.py and tests/unit/test_eval_budget.py: the live planner's request, repair, usage and budget handling against a recording fake transport. No provider is called.
not_numerical.live_provider: Never run under prompt 2.1.0 or 2.2.0. The last live results (2026-09-25) are for earlier prompt text.
